headline: Five libraries give Ward 39 the second highest total in Chicago.
summary:
Libraries are Ward 39's standout, with the second highest count anywhere in Chicago. Its houses of worship also span one of the widest ranges of religious traditions in the city. Add faster than typical building permits and a larger than typical share of aldermanic menu money spent on parks, and the ward's civic numbers read strong across the board. All of that lands Ward 39 12th of 50 wards overall, solidly in the top third of the city. It covers North Park, Forest Glen, Albany Park, and Irving Park, on the city's Northwest Side.

The weak points sit in schools and in the kind of places that bring people together outside their own block. Per-pupil school spending sits at the very bottom of the fifty wards. Licensed music and dance venues are among the scarcest in the city, and a modeled estimate, not a headcount, puts the share of residents seeing friends weekly well below most other wards. Over half the ward's park water fountains also carry a history of elevated lead readings, a bigger share than in almost any other ward. Together, the numbers describe a ward that is steady on the basics of city government but thin on nightlife and casual social contact.
reading_the_rankings: A couple of these numbers deserve a second look. Alder attendance for the current council session lands third of 50, which sounds strong, but part of this record predates the 2023 remap, so the figure blends today's ward lines with whoever held the seat before boundaries changed, and the source marks the underlying number medium confidence. Park spending from the aldermanic menu fund also lands third, though the caveat here is different. On this measure, the typical middle-of-the-city range is barely a third of a point wide, so a small shift in dollars can jump a ward several spots. The weaker rankings carry their own caveat too. The estimate that only 16.6 percent of residents see friends weekly comes from a model built on national survey data and the ward's own demographics. Nothing here was counted door to door, and the source flags it low confidence besides.

news.headline: Art Institute's 'Project Windows' Gets Boost From NW Side Businesses
news.note: Six spots across the ward, including Superdawg and the Edgebrook branch library, are displaying local artwork this summer as part of the Art Institute's annual Project Windows program.

news.headline: Police SWAT Team Officer, Woman Shot In Albany Park: 'Absolutely Tragic'
news.note: A police SWAT officer and a 67-year-old woman were shot during a domestic incident and hostage situation in Albany Park, and a suspect was later taken into custody.

news.headline: Protesters Want ICE Out After Chaotic Albany Park Arrest: 'Midway Blitz Is Over, But ICE Has Not Left'
news.note: About 150 people rallied in Horner Park after federal immigration agents made a chaotic arrest at Lawrence and Kedzie in Albany Park.
